senses.gloss: To make someone think of another person or thing because of a likeness.
examples: You *remind* me of my younger brother.
The smell *reminded* her of her grandmother's kitchen.
That song has always *reminded* me of summer camp.

senses.gloss: To force someone out of a job or an official position.
examples: The board voted to *remove* the chief executive.
Two officers were *removed* from duty during the investigation.
Congress has *removed* only a handful of federal judges.

senses.gloss: To cause someone or something to be in a particular condition.
examples: The injury *rendered* him unable to walk for a month.
One bad storm can *render* the road impassable.
The new law has *rendered* the old permits worthless.

senses.gloss: To give or deliver help, a service, or a formal judgment.
examples: He sent an invoice for services *rendered*.
Passing ships are required to *render* assistance.
The jury *rendered* its verdict after three hours.

senses.gloss: To melt the fat out of meat by cooking it slowly.
examples: *Render* the bacon fat over low heat.
She *rendered* the duck fat and saved it for the potatoes.
Cook the pork belly until the fat has *rendered*.

senses.gloss: To start something again with new energy after it has stopped.
senses.ru: возобновлять, возобновить; начинать с новой силой
examples: The report will *renew* pressure on the company to act.
She *renewed* her efforts to find a job.
Talks are being *renewed* after a long break.

senses.gloss: To make someone feel strong dislike or disgust.
examples: The violence in the film *repelled* her.
His table manners *repel* everyone in the office.
I was *repelled* by the smell before I even opened the door.

senses.gloss: To push something away by a force, or to keep it from getting in.
senses.ru: отталкивать (о магнитах); отпугивать, не пропускать (воду, насекомых)
examples: Two magnets facing the same way *repel* each other.
The spray *repelled* the mosquitoes all evening.
This fabric is very good at *repelling* water.

senses.gloss: To put something back in the place where it belongs.
senses.ru: класть на место, ставить обратно; вернуть на место
examples: Please *replace* the cap tightly after use.
He *replaced* the book on the shelf and left.
She read the letter twice before *replacing* it in the envelope.

senses.gloss: To go through an event again in your mind.
senses.ru: мысленно прокручивать, снова и снова переживать
examples: I keep *replaying* that conversation in my head.
He *replayed* the accident over and over for weeks.
Try not to *replay* every mistake before you fall asleep.

senses.gloss: For a cell or a virus to make copies of itself.
examples: The virus *replicates* quickly in the lungs.
The cells *replicated* faster than the drug could stop them.
The vaccine keeps the virus from *replicating*.

senses.gloss: To tell the police or another authority about a crime or about someone's wrongdoing.
examples: You should *report* the theft right away.
A neighbor *reported* him to the police.
The leak was never *reported* to the authorities.

senses.gloss: To work under a particular manager in a company.
examples: She *reports* directly to the head of sales.
For two years I *reported* to a manager in Chicago.
The three new engineers will be *reporting* to you.

senses.gloss: To go to a place and present yourself for work or duty.
senses.ru: являться, явиться (на службу, на место); прибыть
examples: *Report* to the front desk when you arrive.
He *reported* for duty at six in the morning.
All new hires are *reporting* to the training room today.

senses.gloss: To be a sign or a symbol of something.
examples: On the map, a blue line *represents* a river.
The artist said the broken chain *represented* freedom.
Nothing in the design is meant to *represent* a real building.

senses.gloss: To amount to a particular quantity or to constitute something.
examples: Women *represent* about half of the students in the program.
Last year's storms *represented* the worst losses in a decade.
That figure *represents* a ten percent increase over last year.

senses.gloss: For a living thing to produce young.
examples: Rabbits *reproduce* very quickly.
The fish *reproduced* in the warm shallow water.
Pandas have trouble *reproducing* in captivity.

senses.gloss: To hold something back for a special purpose or for later.
examples: *Reserve* a cup of the pasta water before you drain it.
The company *reserves* the right to cancel the order.
I'm *reserving* judgment until I hear both sides.

senses.gloss: To make yourself accept something unpleasant that you cannot change.
examples: She *resigned* herself to another year in the same job.
You have to *resign* yourself to the fact that he isn't coming back.
By then we were *resigned* to losing the deposit.

senses.gloss: To stop yourself from doing or taking something you want.
examples: I couldn't *resist* a second slice of cake.
She *resisted* the urge to answer him.
He has never been good at *resisting* a bargain.

senses.gloss: For a material to stay undamaged by something that would normally harm it.
senses.ru: быть устойчивым к, не поддаваться (жару, коррозии)
examples: Stainless steel *resists* rust better than iron.
The coating *resisted* the salt water all winter.
We need a fabric capable of *resisting* heat.

senses.gloss: To place something on a support, or to lean against something for support.
examples: *Rest* your arm on the pillow.
He *rested* his elbows on the table.
The ladder was *resting* against the fence.

senses.gloss: To bring back a service, a right, or a state of affairs that had stopped.
examples: Crews worked all night to *restore* power to the city.
The surgery *restored* most of his hearing.
Order had been *restored* by the time we arrived.

senses.gloss: To put files or settings back from a saved copy.
examples: You can *restore* the whole folder from yesterday's backup.
I *restored* the phone to its factory settings.
The database is being *restored* right now.

senses.gloss: To continue to have or keep something.
examples: The jacket *retains* its shape after washing.
She *retained* control of the company after the sale.
The building has *retained* its original windows.

senses.gloss: To hire a lawyer or another professional by paying in advance.
examples: You should *retain* a lawyer before you sign anything.
The family *retained* a well-known attorney.
He has *retained* the same accountant for twenty years.

senses.gloss: To take something out of use for good.
senses.ru: выводить из эксплуатации, списывать; изымать из обращения
examples: The airline is *retiring* its oldest planes this year.
The team *retired* his number the season after he left.
That software has been *retired* and is no longer supported.

senses.gloss: To pull something back in, or to move back inside.
examples: A cat can *retract* its claws.
The landing gear *retracted* as the plane climbed.
The roof is slowly *retracting* to let in the sun.

senses.gloss: To do the same thing back to someone.
examples: I'll *return* the favor someday.
He waved, and she *returned* the wave.
Thanks for *returning* my call so quickly.

senses.gloss: To produce a profit for the money that was invested.
examples: The fund *returned* eight percent last year.
These bonds *return* very little at the moment.
The project is *returning* less than we hoped.

senses.gloss: To uncover something so that it can be seen.
examples: He pulled back the sheet to *reveal* a new motorcycle.
The X-ray *revealed* a hairline fracture.
The curtain rose, *revealing* an empty stage.

senses.gloss: To officially change an earlier decision or ruling to the opposite.
examples: The appeals court *reversed* the conviction.
The school board may *reverse* the policy next month.
That ruling has since been *reversed*.

senses.gloss: To give a public opinion in writing about a book, a movie, a restaurant, or a product.
examples: She *reviews* restaurants for the local paper.
Critics *reviewed* the album kindly.
The book has been *reviewed* in every major paper.

senses.gloss: To go over material again in order to prepare for a test.
examples: I need to *review* chapter four before the quiz.
We *reviewed* the vocabulary all weekend.
She spent the night *reviewing* her notes.

senses.gloss: To go to a place again after being away for a long time.
senses.ru: снова посещать, побывать снова (в каком-л. месте)
examples: We'd love to *revisit* Chicago in the fall.
He *revisited* the town where he grew up.
I've never *revisited* the school since graduation.

senses.gloss: To make someone feel sick or disgusted.
examples: The smell of the fish *revolted* her.
Cruelty to animals *revolts* most people.
I was *revolted* by what I saw in the video.

senses.gloss: To fit something out with equipment, ropes, or sails.
examples: They *rigged* the boat before dawn.
The truck is *rigged* with a winch and two floodlights.
The crew spent two days *rigging* the lights above the stage.

senses.gloss: For a sound, a feeling, or an effect to spread gradually through a group or a place.
examples: A laugh *rippled* through the audience.
The layoffs will *ripple* through the whole town.
News of the merger is still *rippling* across the industry.

senses.gloss: For a phone to use another company's network while you are away from home.
senses.ru: работать в роуминге, находиться в роуминге
examples: My phone *roams* on a Mexican network near the border.
We *roamed* on a local carrier the whole trip.
Check the rates before your phone starts *roaming* overseas.

senses.gloss: To move very fast with a loud deep noise.
senses.ru: проноситься с рёвом, мчаться с грохотом
examples: A motorcycle *roared* past the house.
The train *roars* through the station without stopping.
We heard trucks *roaring* down the highway all night.
